do_not_regress: Use AST-assisted heuristic split audit as read-only evidence when available.
Keep AST audit outputs in daily-work staging, not project root.
Use multi-island candidate queue at module start.
Allow at most two independent islands in one patch.
Use non-conflicting write checks rather than impossible no-shared-read checks.
Do not stack multiple ZIP patches before validation/freeze.
Allow outer patch-train delivery bundles only as packaging for separate governed patch ZIPs.
Keep every inner patch in a patch train on its own install -> validate -> freeze sequence.
Do not freeze a patch train as one vague outer-bundle entry.
Do not proceed to later train patches if an earlier inner patch fails.

Allow up to four ordered patch ZIPs in one sequential double-refactor delivery train only when each inner ZIP is independently installable, validatable, contract-checkable, freeze-preppable, previewable, and freezeable.
Keep the default maximum at two related refactor slices per inner ZIP.
Individually validate and individually freeze every inner ZIP before the next ZIP is installed.
Do not freeze a sequential delivery train as one outer-bundle memory entry.
Treat the 400-line ideal as a practical target band, not a mandate to atomize files.
Avoid unnecessary micro-files; do not create tiny helper modules merely to reduce line count.
Prefer cohesive helper modules around 250-400 lines when the responsibility naturally fits.
Use ordinary importable .py files for runtime/source logic; ZIP payload folders are delivery packaging only.
Stop a refactor train with a completion guard when remaining helper modules are cohesive and below the 400-line ideal.
title: Large Module Creation and Refactor Protocol
